edit.description: `predicate_from_row`'s `extent` arm (line 679) hard-codes `whole: false`, so no lock row can ever lift the whole grain. Read the grain off the row's new column instead. Two extent clauses on one kind reduce to one `clause_label` today (`skill.extent`), so the grain must distinguish the label the way `when_label_field` composes its guard's value set into the `field` argument.

`ClauseRow` carries no `whole` column; add it beside `unit`, written in `ClauseRow::to_table` and read in `ClauseRow::from_table` — the same codec pair, one `opt_str` lift. Symbols, not line numbers: the three cites had shifted +3 and then back -3 across two windows, and every name resolves by `rg`.
`extent(unit, bound)` (line 154) is the only authoring spelling and offers no grain argument — the author cannot say 'the selection's summed extent'.
the clause-row synthesis (around line 151, where `unit` is written for an `extent` predicate) writes the new column.
ts-rs regeneration of the widened row — machine-written, re-emitted, never hand-edited.

the whole-grain cases — the `selection` helper (line 47) and `whole_grain_bounds_the_selections_summed_extent_in_both_units` (86-108) — construct `Predicate::Extent { whole: true }` by hand; they gain a round-trip through the real writer and reader, per the seam-gate bar.
the clause-row codec round-trip gains the new column.

summary: `extent`'s whole grain is judged but unauthorable: no lock column and no SDK spelling carry it, so every decoded extent clause is each-grain.
